name: Sonnet concentrated AI/technology
strategy: Concentrated long book in AI infrastructure leaders (compute, networking, memory) with leveraged semis beta for extra torque, a modest single-name short to offset gross exposure, and cash held for weekly rebalancing flexibility.

positions.thesis: Core AI compute bottleneck; despite the 3-day semis selloff (China chip-smuggling headline, sector rotation), analyst targets imply ~59% upside and quality-name accumulation (Cathie Wood buying the dip) continues. Highest-quality way to own the capex cycle; hold core size through the volatility.

Just posted a blowout quarter: Azure +41% (fastest growth in four years, crossed $100B annualized), revenue and EPS beat consensus, stock up ~9% after hours. Extending data-center useful life (15->25yr) trims near-term capex guide but is margin-accretive, not a demand cut. Best risk-adjusted AI-platform exposure this week; increasing weight to the strongest confirmed catalyst in the book.

Custom silicon/networking diversifies compute exposure beyond GPUs; new $200B multi-year Samsung memory/AI-chip collaboration through 2030 is a bullish structural catalyst even as the stock sold off with the sector this week.

MI-series share gains and the new Core Scientific datacenter deal (~2.5GW, ~$14B) remain real catalysts, but trimming from 10% to 7% given a stretched ~143x PE and AMD carrying the highest beta into a sector-wide rotation out of chip stocks.

HBM/memory structurally tight long-term (cheap on trailing PE ~18x) but trimming from 10% to 5% given a brutal -9.94% single-day move, -32% drawdown from June highs, CEO insider selling into the dip, and direct China memory-competition headlines (ChangXin) that are name-specific risk on top of the sector selloff.

reassessment_note: Unrestricted-retail resize (2026-07-30, free internet + no sizing caps): Covering the AAPL short: the 'relative AI-monetization laggard' thesis is empirically dead — AAPL just hit a $5T market cap, surpassed NVDA as the world's most valuable company, sits near its 52-week high, and reports earnings after today's close with the market pricing strong iPhone demand; staying short into that is fighting the tape on a broken thesis, not honoring conviction. Simultaneously the semis complex is in a genuine 3-day rout (SMH -4.79% today, sector described as 'bear-market territory', China chip-equipment competition headlines, AI-capex-sustainability worries) — real risk, but the underlying capex story is not broken: MSFT just printed Azure +41% growth, beat on revenue/EPS, and popped ~9% after hours; Meta raised its FY26 capex minimum; Amazon guides to a record ~$200B capex year. That combination (mega-cap AI demand still accelerating, chip stocks merely repricing risk) argues for staying long quality AI infrastructure rather than fleeing, while trimming the two names carrying the most idiosyncratic/valuation risk right now: AMD (PE ~143x, most beta-heavy) and MU (-32% from its June peak, CEO sold ~$37M of stock into the selloff, direct China memory-competition headline risk). Freed capital from the short + trims goes partly to MSFT (best fundamental catalyst of the week) and partly to cash, both to cushion further semis downside and preserve the mandate's weekly-rebalancing flexibility given the book is already down -6.44% NAV with a -10.74% max drawdown.
research_notes: Researched live prices/news (via WebFetch on stockanalysis.com and other sources, WebSearch budget was exhausted session-wide before I could use it) for both books as of the Jul 29-30, 2026 close. Round-2 findings: semis in a 3-day rout, SMH -4.79% on the day and described as 'bear-market territory' (China chip-equipment competition, AI-capex-sustainability worries, Taiwan chip-smuggling investigation touching an NVDA employee); NVDA -3.55%, AVGO -2.78%, AMD -5.51%, MU -9.94% (-32% off its June peak, CEO sold ~$37M stock into the dip). Countervailing bullish signal: MSFT beat hard (Azure +41%, revenue/EPS beat, stock +~9% after hours) and mega-cap capex guides (Meta raising its FY26 capex floor, Amazon guiding to a record ~$200B) show AI demand still accelerating even as chip-stock sentiment sours. Most important finding: AAPL, which the book was short as a 'relative AI-monetization laggard,' instead just became the most valuable company in the world (~$5T market cap, briefly passed NVDA), sits near its 52-week high, and reports earnings after today's close with strong iPhone demand expected - the short thesis is falsified, so I closed it. Round-3 findings: the standing round-3 book (GOOGL/AMZN/META/PLTR/CRWD long, SMH short) is itself an AI/semis book that contradicts its own stated mandate of cross-sector momentum avoiding AI/semis; META also just badly missed EPS on a Q2 report and cratered ~7% after hours on capex/Reality-Labs-loss concerns, reinforcing that the round-3 book's actual AI exposure was working against it too. I found genuine confirmed-breakout signals in XBI (biotech, +72% 1yr, breakout language, record M&A, rotation-out-of-tech safe haven) and KRE (regional banks, +26% YTD, near highs, strong Q2 fundamentals) for the long side, and genuine confirmed-breakdown signals in GDX (gold miners, -37% off 52wk high, bearish technicals) and TLT (long bonds, near 52wk lows, structural downtrend on rising yields) for the short side. Could not confirm a crypto breakdown (BTC data read as consolidating, not trending down), so I left crypto out rather than force it.
